The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: to want something to happen.

draft.emotion: optimistic and looking forward to the future with quiet confidence
notes: Followed by a comma and the conjunction że ('that') when introducing a clause: Mam nadzieję, że... ('I hope that...').
Can also be used on its own as a response: Mam nadzieję! ('I hope so!').

senses.definition: To want something to happen and think that it is possible.

examples.text: Mam nadzieję, że pogoda jutro będzie ładna.
examples.translation: I hope that the weather will be nice tomorrow.
examples.emotion: hopeful and eager for a sunny day

draftBefore.shortGloss: to hope; to want something to happen
draftBefore.emotion: optimistic and looking forward to the future with quiet confidence
notes: Mieć nadzieję is followed by the conjunction że when introducing a clause, or used on its own.
Do not confuse it with chcieć, which simply means to want something directly without the forward-looking expectation of hope.

senses.definition: To believe and want that something desirable will happen.

examples.text: Mam nadzieję, że pogoda jutro będzie ładna.
examples.translation: I hope that the weather will be nice tomorrow.
examples.emotion: hopeful and eager for a sunny day

senses.definition: To strongly want something to happen in the future.

examples.text: Mam nadzieję, że wszystko dobrze się skończy.
examples.translation: I want everything to turn out well.
examples.emotion: reassuring and earnest about a positive outcome

faults.quote: To strongly want something to happen in the future.
faults.why: Artificial split; 'mieć nadzieję' only means 'to hope', not 'to want'.

faults.why: Translating 'mieć nadzieję' as 'to want' confuses learners with 'chcieć' (contradicting note 1).
